THE ALPHA QUESTION, SETTLED AGAINST THE BOARD AND AGAINST A CALCULATOR. The
board fills the bar `--color/bg-overlay` = rgba(17,24,39,0.5); the code runs
0.75. `lib.mjs` drops alpha before comparing (Figma cannot export a layer
opacity), so both read #111827 and the join passes either way — which means
the diff CANNOT decide this and the contrast sweep has to. At 0.5 over a light
canvas the bar composites to #888C93; at 0.75 to #4D525D. The code's own
comment already records that a previous claim of 6.99:1 was really 1.34:1 for
exactly this reason. Everything on the bar is legible at 0.75 and the
secondary labels would not be at 0.5, so the code's 0.75 stands and the
board's 0.5 is recorded here rather than adopted. The founder's question in
the brief — verify the breadcrumb fix against this board — answers: the fix is
right, and the board is where the 0.5 came from.
